main_body: Sci-fi control tower: a hipped roof slope over a window band, a grey shaft, and a wider base with its own sloped roof over a front wall with a door
top_band: Column x=24, rows 2-16: a blue-grey sloped roof, mid tone L118 at rows 2-9, L148 at rows 10-14, lightest L178 at rows 15-16. A step to the dark front face follows at row 17-18. The lower base has a similar sloped roof band at rows 52-61.
evidence: Both the upper roof and the lower base roof are wide trapezoid slopes that read as lighter horizontal surfaces seen from above. In the middle column the light slope (L118-178) ends in a lightest edge row at rows 15-16. Below it come dark rows (L34) forming an eave shadow over the window band, which is the front face at rows 18-29. The windows sit in dark inset frames, and the door at the bottom is recessed with a dark frame. The shaft between the two roofs is a vertical face, which is normal for a tower. All major parts keep the top-plus-front structure.

style.evidence: The roof has about 4-5 steps and the windows have some dither, so the shading is not shallow. The outline is mostly neutral near-black (#06070e, #1c2230), and 84% of dark edge pixels are neutral against 7-9% in the references, which gives the sticker look. The shaft, the lower wall panels and the dark front areas are large flat fills (21% coverage against 0% in both references). The piece has only 31 distinct colours against 66 and 185 in the references. Its median of 10 colours per tile is close to the stone reference's 11, but it lacks the per-tile grain and texture of the references. Overall it is flatter and more sticker-like than the references.
